issue.title: Operability basics: health endpoints, structured JSON logs with request IDs, graceful shutdown, a first runbook (R12)

data.no_adr_reason:
None of spec 0006's decisions needs a new ADR. Each one either applies an ADR we already have or is cheap to change.

The decisions that are significant and hard to reverse are already recorded in ADR 0015 (accepted). It covers Actuator with Micrometer/Prometheus and Spring Boot's structured JSON logging, and rejects OpenTelemetry and hand-written health checks. It also fixes the separate management port 8081, readiness meaning the database is reachable and migrated and the Click queue isn't saturated, and liveness, the per-route HTTP and domain metrics, and a request ID generated when missing and returned as a header. The rule that Long URLs, Manage Tokens and raw user agents are never logged comes from ADRs 0015, 0013 and 0014. Keeping the SQLite pool, WAL mode and busy timeout fixed is ADR 0021, and the Click flush timeout on shutdown is ADR 0012.

The rest of the spec applies those ADRs and fails the bar on at least one count (hard to reverse, surprising, a real trade-off):
- Graceful shutdown and its order use Spring Boot's own lifecycle, plus the Click Recorder's existing SmartLifecycle phase.
- These are configuration values the spec itself lists under "Decided while writing this spec, all easy to change":
  - the X-Request-Id header name and the 64-character safe-ID rule
  - ECS as the JSON format and the LOG_FORMAT json/text switch
  - one access line per request at INFO
  - SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT defaulting to 10s
  - "saturated" meaning the queue is completely full (Further Notes says a threshold or hold time later is a configuration change, not a new ADR)
  - the PORT+81 default in local.sh
- Checking BASE_URL and the CLICK_* settings at startup only rejects values that already produce broken Short URLs or a broken Click Recorder.
- Naming the rejecting Rule in RuleResult.Rejected is an additive change inside the existing rules module (ADR 0004).
- Leaving the management port without authentication matches ADR 0015 (protection by where it sits on the network). The spec lists adding authentication as out of scope and says it would need a new decision then.

The spec also says "No new ADR expected. ADR 0015 already decides the tooling, the separate port, the health groups and the log rules."
